messages:
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout r-2026-03-15-12:20 to staging (20% traffic)

deploy-bot: metrics: lat=40ms p95, errors=0.4% (baseline 0.3%)

incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate in staging canary (rule: canary-5xx-threshold). paging oncall: @julie :rotating_light:

julie: on it. seeing alerts in cloudwatch dashboard. linking: https://redwood.metrics/staging/canary/1928765432

sre_marc: I see a spike in HTTP 502/504 from the auth proxy at 12:22:31. sample logs:
```
502 GET /v1/generate 45.12.3.6 - "upstream terminated connection"
504 upstream read timeout from runtime (kv-cache)
```

julie: tagging platform team @platform_lina. rolling back if blast radius grows above 5% errors or latency > 800ms p95

platform_lina: looking. initial hunch: kernel-level socket backlog on the new runtime kernel arg. congrats to the deploy team for fast canary though. can we pin traffic to previous revision while we triage?

julie: initiating abort criteria now. aborting canary cutover, running kill-switch for rollout r-2026-03-15-12:20.

julie: command run:
```
# feature-flag CLI
redwood ff set rollout/r-2026-03-15-12:20 enabled false --env staging --actor julie
```

deploy-bot: acknowledged. Feature flag rollout/r-2026-03-15-12:20 set to false by julie at 12:23:05. routing reverted to previous model variant. starting automated rollback job id rb-7721

deploy-bot: rollback in progress: draining canary instances, switching traffic back to r-2026-03-10 stable (expected duration ~90s)

customer_ash: alert from CS — one staging customer tests running load saw failures but no production customers impacted. confirming no support tickets yet. noting for postmortem.

sre_marc: after rollback traffic normalized within ~45s. p95 latency back to 42ms, errors down to 0.3%. collecting traces and spans for 12:21-12:24 window. attaching sample trace ids: trace-A12, trace-B47

julie: summary for incident timeline:
- 12:20: deploy started (canary 20%)
- 12:22: 5xx observed in canary auth proxy
- 12:23: abort criteria met (>5% of canary requests failing for 2 consecutive minute windows)
- 12:23: feature flag kill-switch toggled by julie
- 12:24: rollback job started, traffic reverted to stable
- 12:25: metrics normalized

eng_cory: nice and quick response. can we capture exact abort rule that fired? want to cross-check thresholds in the rollout config.

platform_lina: abort rule = {"error_rate_threshold_pct":5, "window_secs":120, "consecutive_windows":2}. will add config link to the rollout record.

sre_marc: adding logs snippet for ops channel:
```
12:22:18 auth-proxy[pid]: upstream conn reset, retrying
12:22:32 runtime[pid]: kv-cache miss leading to long-tail open retry
12:22:35 proxy[pid]: returning 502 to client after upstream failure
```

customer_ash: CS note: flagged internal staging-only test accounts; no P1 customer impact. will monitor for any out-of-band reports.

julie: handoff note to next oncall (night shift): issue mitigated by rollback and flag off. artifacts to review: rollout config, kernel arg diff, runtime k8s pod events, traces for trace-A12/B47. please run a quick smoke of auth flows after you take over. tagging next_oncall.

deploy-bot: rollback completed successfully at 12:24:37. stable revision r-2026-03-10 serving 100% traffic.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0315-21 (severity: S2, status: resolved -> monitoring). responders: julie, sre_marc, platform_lina, eng_cory, customer_ash.

julie: quick retrospective notes: 1) abort rule behaved as intended, 2) need clearer pre-rollout perf probe for auth proxy, 3) add a canary-level synthetic that exercises kv-cache path. filing follow-up tasks.

eng_cory: agree. can we schedule a 30m blameless sync tomorrow to decide whether to rework kernel arg or revert longer-term? I'll create a RFC draft.

platform_lina: I'll open a tracking ticket for the kernel arg change and add steps for preflight checks.

sre_marc: dropping CI traces and pod events into the incident folder: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0315-21/logs

julie: locking thread. leaving handoff: next oncall please ack in #eng-oncall when you pick this up. :white_check_mark:

(next_oncall): acked. picking up monitoring and next steps at 18:00 PST.

customer_ash: no customer-facing comms required at this time. will update if anything changes.

julie: great work team. thanks for fast mitigation.
